A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DVC is the site where the brain detects the energy imbalance that occurs during hypoglycaemia, and that this is done by the detection of a change in lactate.
the female rat Dorsal vagal complex (the hindbrain region responsible for detecting and responding to hypoglycemics) is sensitive to the effects of insulin and estradiol.
the effects of estradiol on glucose metabolism are not restricted to peripheral tissues, but are also evident in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
estrogen enhances lactate uptake by the brain and that this effect is important in preventing the brain from detecting low glucose levels.
estrogen enhances the ability of the brain to respond to low glucose levels by increasing the number of transporters in the brain for glucose and lactate, which are the primary fuels of the brain.
